cr08_nonperformative.notes: tests/test_court_import_gate.py: 45/45 PASSED (plus test_hook_blocks_staged_court_market_import in test_githooks). Independent naives confirm the EXISTING reds are real teeth: body_only misses nested_*/importlib/exec; rel_always_ok misses both relative-escape tests; first_alias_only misses multi_alias_second; full_dotted false-flags scipy.stats while real gate does not. CR-08 failure mode is NOT 'tests that don't discriminate' — it is the same prior-tooth pattern: enum named major vectors, red tests never written, gate still green.

new_findings.what: symlinked-dir-carrier (enum major): court/sub -> ../adapters is invisible to scan_court (os.walk followlinks=False, only flags .py file symlinks) AND to --staged (mode 120000 path court/sub has no .py suffix so _staged_court_paths drops it). from court.sub import qlib_cn is top-level 'court' → allow. Both paths PASS while runtime loads adapters market code. Classic named-but-untested.
new_findings.snippet_or_cmd: tmpdir: ln -s adapters court/sub; court/judge3.py='from court.sub import qlib_cn'; adapters/qlib_cn.py='import qlib'; scan_court→[]; --staged rc=0 PASS
new_findings.fix: Fail-closed on ANY symlink under court/ (file or directory) in walk + staged (ls-files mode 120000 for any court/** path, not only *.py); red-test exactly the enum fixture.

new_findings.what: V06 incomplete: secondary Name rebind after from-import is not tracked. from importlib import import_module; im=import_module; im('qlib') and imp=__import__; imp('qlib') and f=il.import_module; f('qlib') all PASS. Red tests only cover import_module as imp direct call and il.import_module Attribute form — not Assign rebind. Enum V06 example even listed getattr(importlib,'import_module')('qlib') which also PASSes.
new_findings.snippet_or_cmd:
check_source("from importlib import import_module
im = import_module
im('qlib')
") → []; check_source("imp = __import__
imp('qlib')
") → []; check_source("import importlib
f=importlib.import_module
f('qlib')
") → []
new_findings.fix: Either (a) simple def-use: any Name assigned from import_module/__import__ or Attribute *.import_module is a dynamic-import callee; or (b) honest-ceiling: document Assign/getattr/partial as out-of-scope and stop claiming 'rebound' closed in commit.

new_findings.what: V14 (enum minor, practically major hole next to V06): builtins.__import__('qlib'), import builtins as b; b.__import__('qlib'), getattr(builtins,'__import__')(...), vars(importlib)['import_module'](...), importlib.__dict__['import_module']('qlib'), functools.partial(importlib.import_module,'qlib'), operator.methodcaller — all PASS. Enum required flag OR document as accepted blind spot; neither red test nor docstring lists these spellings (only coarse exec/non-literal).
new_findings.snippet_or_cmd:
check_source("import builtins
builtins.__import__('qlib')
") → []; check_source("from builtins import __import__ as bi
bi('qlib')
") → []
new_findings.fix: Flag Attribute attr in {__import__,import_module,exec,eval,compile} on any receiver; and/or document V14 class as declared-limit with a red test that asserts PASS + ceiling text.

new_findings.what: exec/eval/compile only matched as bare ast.Name — builtins.exec('import qlib') and e=eval; e('...') PASS. Bare exec/eval/compile are flagged (coarse heuristic works for the happy spelling only).
new_findings.fix: Match Call with Attribute.attr in {exec,eval,compile} as well as Name; or tighten honesty text to 'bare-name exec/eval/compile only'.

new_findings.what: Enum dynamic-importlib listed spec_from_file_location as a bypass to flag; design left 'flag presence?' open; implementation does NOT flag it (nor SourceFileLoader/runpy.run_module). Commit honesty correctly parks spec_from_file out of scope — but enum+commit still market 'dynamic import closed' without the third arm of the enum red_test.
new_findings.fix: Either denylist spec_from_file_location/module_from_spec/runpy.run_* in court, or add declared-limit red test asserting PASS + docstring bullet (commit already claims out-of-scope).

new_findings.what: design-decisions.md and commit simplify relative rules to 'level≥2 = escape'. True only for package depth-1 (court/*.py). From court/sub/deep, from ...adapters resolves to court.adapters (top=court) and correctly PASSes; escape needs ....adapters. Code resolver is right; the prose overclaims. Not a functional hole for flat court/ today.
new_findings.snippet_or_cmd: check_source('from ...adapters import c\n', 'court/sub/deep/x.py') → PASSED; check_source('from ....adapters import c\n', 'court/sub/deep/x.py') → FLAGGED
new_findings.fix: Rewrite relative rule as 'resolve against file package parts; flag iff resolved top-level not allowlisted' — drop absolute 'level≥2'.

new_findings.what: import __main__ is flagged (__main__ ∉ sys.stdlib_module_names on CPython 3.12.8). Unlikely in court/; noise only.
new_findings.snippet_or_cmd: python -c "import sys; print('__main__' in sys.stdlib_module_names)" → False; check_source('import __main__\n') → FLAGGED
new_findings.fix: Allowlist __main__ if ever needed, or ignore.

new_findings.what: Top-level reduction reverse: import numpy.qlib_market / from scipy import qlib_hack PASS (top=numpy/scipy). Not a true market-lib import — cannot load qlib via numpy namespace without a real submodule. Declared by allowlist design; numpy_finance correctly FLAGGED (exact top, not prefix). No action beyond not overselling.
new_findings.fix: None for import gate; keep as declared (namespace fiction ≠ shipping market code).

relative_import_resolution: Resolver matches Python package semantics. pkg=court.sub.deep, level=3 module=adapters → top 'court' (court.adapters) ALLOW; level=4 → top 'adapters' FLAG. from .. import adapters at court root FLAGs; mixed from . import dsr, adapters at court root all resolve under court ALLOW. Planting court/adapters/*.py with import qlib IS caught by recursive scan (user.py importing court.adapters alone is fine). Hole is NOT wrong relative math — it is symlink-dir + court.* allow without scanning through symlinks. Design prose 'level≥2 always escapes' is wrong for depth>1; code is fine.
dynamic_import_alias_gaps: from importlib import import_module; im = import_module; im('qlib')
from importlib import import_module as imp; im = imp; im('qlib')
from builtins import __import__ as bi; bi('qlib')
runpy.run_module('qlib') / run_path (stdlib import allowed; call untracked)
honesty_ceiling: Strong on the main point: module docstring + commit HONEST CEILING state import≠semantic decoupling (runtime cal object, 252/10%, hard path); tests test_runtime_object_injection_not_seen / test_hardcoded_market_constant_not_seen lock PASS+docs. exec/eval/compile presence flagged and labeled coarse in docstring — but only bare Name, which is not fully disclosed. spec_from_file/sys.path/.pyx parked out-of-scope in commit (good). Design still has unresolved 'flag presence?' for spec_from — implementation chose not to flag without a declared-limit red test. No evidence of selling the gate as full market-agnostic proof; README iron-law line is product intent, not gate overclaim. Residual overclaim is dynamic-import 'closed' language vs half coverage of enum V06/V14/symlink-dir.
stdlib_version_note: CPython 3.12.8 conda-forge, len(sys.stdlib_module_names)=301. No market top-level (qlib/baostock/akshare/tushare/pandas/yfinance/…) appears in the set → no false-allow via stdlib collision. antigravity/this/cgi are in-set and ALLOW — reasonable (not market). __main__ NOT in set → minor false-flag. Version-drift risk (tomllib etc.) is documented in design; this interpreter is the reference. No concrete market-name false-allow found on this machine.
strongest: Allowlist + top-level reduction keeps the real court/ silent day-one; ast.walk catches nested/TYPE_CHECKING/try; multi-alias on alias.name; staged scans git show :path not worktree; file-level fail-closed (SyntaxError/non-UTF8/unreadable/.py symlink); pre-commit 1b wiring; and an unusually honest semantic-decoupling ceiling with locking tests.
weakest_link: CR-08 recurrence: 63-vector enum named major carriers (symlinked-dir-carrier, V06 getattr/rebind, V14 builtins indirection) then shipped with red tests only for the easy spellings — those vectors still green end-to-end. A gate that only bites textbook import qlib is a speed bump, not a tooth.
